subject: math
title: Grade 7 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions
seo_title: Grade 7 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Area Models, Reciprocals, Mixed Numbers (Free, Answer Key, Ontario)
standard_text: Multiply and divide fractions by fractions, using tools in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing fractions for the Ontario curriculum: area models, simplifying before you multiply, how many fit, multiplying by the reciprocal, mixed numbers and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators and the denominators. To divide, multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction.
key_sub: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2. 2/3 ÷ 4/5 = 2/3 × 5/4 = 5/6: flip only the fraction you divide by. Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first.
body_html:
The big idea

× a fraction means “of”. 23 × 34 means 23 of 34. ÷ a fraction asks “how many fit?” 56 ÷ 13 asks how many thirds fit in 56.

Multiply fractions

Multiply the numerators. Multiply the denominators. Then simplify. The area model shows why the denominators multiply: the square is cut into 3 × 4 = 12 small rectangles.

Example 1

25 × 37 = ?

2 × 35 × 7 = 635.

Answer: 635

Simplify before you multiply

Divide a numerator and a denominator by the same number first. The numbers stay small.

Example 2

49 × 38 = ?

4 and 8 share 4: they become 1 and 2. 3 and 9 share 3: they become 1 and 3. Now 13 × 12 = 16.

Answer: 16

Divide fractions

Count how many groups fit, or use the rule: keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction (use its reciprocal).

Example 3

23 ÷ 45 = ?

Keep 23, flip 45 to 54: 23 × 1 14 = 1012 = 56. Check: 56 × 45 = 2030 = 23.

Answer: 56

Mixed numbers

Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first. Then multiply or divide.

Example 4

1 12 × 2 23 = ?

Write 1 12 as 32 and 2 23 as 83. 32 × 83 = 246 = 4.

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
23 × 45 = 68 (adding across)Multiply across: 2 × 43 × 5 = 815.
23 ÷ 45 = 32 × 45 (flipping the wrong fraction)Keep the first fraction. Flip only the divisor: 23 × 1 14 = 56.
1 12 × 2 23 = 2 + 12 × 23 = 2 13 (multiplying whole parts and fraction parts separately)Change to improper fractions first: 32 × 83 = 4.
Simplifying two numerators, like 6 and 9 in 67 × 910Always pair a numerator with a denominator: 6 and 10.

faq.q: How do you multiply fractions in Grade 7?
faq.a: Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. For example, 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2. You can also simplify before you multiply by dividing a numerator and a denominator by the same number.

faq.q: How do you divide a fraction by a fraction?
faq.a: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction, then multiply. For example, 2/3 ÷ 4/5 = 2/3 × 5/4 = 10/12 = 5/6.

faq.q: How do you multiply and divide mixed numbers?
faq.a: Change each mixed number to an improper fraction first. For example, 1 1/2 × 2 2/3 = 3/2 × 8/3 = 4, and 2 1/2 ÷ 1 1/4 = 5/2 × 4/5 = 2.

faq.q: When do Ontario students learn to multiply and divide fractions by fractions?
faq.a: In Grade 7, in the Number strand of the 2020 Ontario math curriculum (expectation B2.8). In Grade 6, students multiply and divide whole numbers by proper fractions.

items.q: The square is 1 whole. The light columns are 34 of the square. The dark part is a part of the light columns. Which multiplication does the dark part show?
c: 13 × 34
13 × 14
13 + 34
23 × 34
items.e: The light part is 3 of 4 columns: 34 of the square. The dark part is 1 of the 3 rows of the light part: 13 of it. So the dark part is 13 of 34, which is 13 × 34 = 14.

items.q: The square is 1 whole. The light columns are 23 of the square. The dark part is a part of the light columns. Which multiplication does the dark part show?
c: 34 × 23
14 + 23
14 × 13
14 × 23
items.e: The light part is 2 of 3 columns: 23 of the square. The dark part is 1 of the 4 rows of the light part: 14 of it. So the dark part is 14 of 23, which is 14 × 23 = 16.

items.q: The model shows 12 × 34. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 2 = 8 equal small rectangles. 3 × 1 = 3 of them are dark. So 12 × 34 = 38. The answer is 38.

items.q: The model shows 25 × 23. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 3 × 5 = 15 equal small rectangles. 2 × 2 = 4 of them are dark. So 25 × 23 = 415. The answer is 415.

items.q: The model shows 12 × 35. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 5 × 2 = 10 equal small rectangles. 3 × 1 = 3 of them are dark. So 12 × 35 = 310. The answer is 310.

items.q: The model shows 12 × 56. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.
items.e: The square is cut into 6 × 2 = 12 equal small rectangles. 5 × 1 = 5 of them are dark. So 12 × 56 = 512. The answer is 512.

items.q: The model shows 13 × 23. What fraction of the whole square is dark? Give the answer in simplest form.

items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 5 = 20 equal small rectangles. 3 × 3 = 9 of them are dark. So 35 × 34 = 920. The answer is 920.

items.e: The square is cut into 5 × 3 = 15 equal small rectangles. 4 × 2 = 8 of them are dark. So 23 × 45 = 815. The answer is 815.

items.q: Simplify before you multiply: 49 × 38. Which is correct after simplifying?
c: 13 × 32
13 × 18
13 × 12
43 × 12
items.e: Pair each numerator with a denominator. 4 and 8 share 4: they become 1 and 2. 3 and 9 share 3: they become 1 and 3. So 49 × 38 becomes 13 × 12 = 16. Each time, divide both numbers of the pair.

items.q: Ethan simplifies 67 × 910 by dividing 6 and 9 by 3 before multiplying. What is wrong?
c: Nothing. You can divide any two numbers.
You can never simplify before multiplying.
6 and 9 are both numerators. Divide a numerator and a denominator.
items.e: Dividing two numerators changes the value. Pair a numerator with a denominator: 6 and 10 share 2. Then 37 × 95 = 2735. 6 and 9 are both numerators, so he cannot divide them both.

items.q: Without calculating, which product is less than 56?
c: 56 × 1 12
56 × 34
56 × 1 13
items.e: Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 gives less than you started with. 34 is less than 1, so 56 × 34 is less than 56. 56 × 1 = 56, and 43 and 32 are greater than 1.

items.q: The bar shows 34. How many groups of 18 fit in 34? 34 ÷ 18 = ?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 1 eighth. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 1 = 6 groups. So 34 ÷ 18 = 6. Check: 6 × 18 = 34.

items.q: The bar shows 23. How many groups of 16 fit in 23? 23 ÷ 16 = ?
items.e: Use sixths: 23 = 46. Each group is 1 sixth. 4 sixths make 4 ÷ 1 = 4 groups. So 23 ÷ 16 = 4. Check: 4 × 16 = 23.

items.q: The bar shows 45. How many groups of 25 fit in 45? 45 ÷ 25 = ?
items.e: Use fifths. Each group is 2 fifths. 4 fifths make 4 ÷ 2 = 2 groups. So 45 ÷ 25 = 2. Check: 2 × 25 = 45.

items.q: The bar shows 56. How many groups of 13 fit in 56? 56 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Use sixths: 13 = 26. Each group is 2 sixths. 5 sixths make 2 full groups, with 1 sixth left over. That 1 sixth is 12 of a group. So 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 13 = 56.

items.q: The bar shows 78. How many groups of 14 fit in 78? 78 ÷ 14 = ?
items.e: Use eighths: 14 = 28. Each group is 2 eighths. 7 eighths make 3 full groups, with 1 eighth left over. That 1 eighth is 12 of a group. So 78 ÷ 14 = 3 12. Check: 3 12 × 14 = 78.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 35?
items.e: Flip the fraction: the reciprocal of 35 is 53. Check: 35 × 53 = 1515 = 1. (−35 is the opposite, not the reciprocal.)

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 2 14?
items.e: First write 2 14 as a fraction: 94. Then flip it: 49. Check: 94 × 49 = 1.

c: 32 × 45
23 × 54
32 × 54

items.e: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second fraction: 23 × 54. Do not flip 23.

items.q: Without calculating, which quotient is greater than 34?
c: 34 ÷ 1 12
34 × 23
34 ÷ 23
items.e: Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a greater answer, because more than one group fits. 23 is less than 1, so 34 ÷ 23 = 1 18 is greater than 34.

items.q: Priya says 23 ÷ 45 = 65. What mistake did she make?
c: She flipped 23 instead of 45.
items.e: 32 × 45 = 1210 = 65, so Priya flipped the first fraction. Flip only the divisor: 23 × 54 = 1012 = 56.

items.q: 34 ÷ ? = 3
items.e: 3 groups fit in 34, so each group is 34 ÷ 3 = 34 × 13 = 14. Check: 34 ÷ 14 = 34 × 4 = 3.

items.q: Write 2 35 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 2 wholes are 2 × 5 = 10 fifths. Add the 3 fifths: 10 + 3 = 13. So 2 35 = 135.

items.q: Write 3 14 as an improper fraction.
items.e: 3 wholes are 3 × 4 = 12 fourths. Add the 1 fourth: 12 + 1 = 13. So 3 14 = 134.

items.q: 1 12 × 2 23 = ?

items.e: Write 3 34 as 154. Write 1 12 as 32. Keep 154, change ÷ to ×, and flip 32 to 23. Simplify first: divide 15 and 3 by 3, and divide 2 and 4 by 2. Now 52 × 1 = 52 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 1 12 = 3 34.

items.e: Write 5 14 as 214. Write 1 34 as 74. Keep 214, change ÷ to ×, and flip 74 to 47. Simplify first: divide 21 and 7 by 7, and the 4s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3. Check: 3 × 1 34 = 5 14.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 2 78 × 4 110?
items.e: Round each mixed number to the nearest whole number: 2 78 is close to 3 and 4 110 is close to 4. 3 × 4 = 12, so the product is about 12. (2 × 4 = 8 ignores the fraction parts.)

items.q: Without calculating, which is true about 3 12 ÷ 1 34?
c: It is equal to 3 12.
It is less than 3 12.
It is greater than 3 12.
items.e: 1 34 is greater than 1, so fewer than 3 12 groups fit. The quotient is less than 3 12: 72 × 47 = 2814 = 2.

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, fabric and trails

items.q: A recipe for butter tarts needs 34 cup of maple syrup. Nathan makes 12 of the recipe. How much maple syrup does he need?
items.e: 12 of 34 means 12 × 34. 12 × 34 = 1 × 32 × 4 = 38 cup.

items.q: One batch of pancakes needs 23 cup of milk. Lucas makes 2 12 batches for a sleepover. How much milk does he need?
items.e: 2 12 batches of 23 cup: multiply. Write 2 12 as 52. Simplify first: the 2s cancel. Now 5 × 13 = 53 = 1 23 cups.

items.q: Ava has 3 34 cups of oats. One batch of granola bars needs 34 cup. How many batches can she make?
items.e: How many 34 cups fit in 3 34 cups? Divide. Write 3 34 as 154. Keep 154, change ÷ to ×, and flip 34 to 43. Simplify first: divide 15 and 3 by 3, and the 4s cancel. Now 5 × 1 = 5 batches. Check: 5 × 34 = 3 34.

items.q: Mateo has 56 m of red fabric for Canada Day banners. Each banner needs 512 m. How many banners can he make?
items.e: How many 512 m pieces fit in 56 m? Divide. Keep 56, change ÷ to ×, and flip 512 to 125. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and divide 12 and 6 by 6. Now 1 × 2 = 2 banners. Check: 2 × 512 = 56.

items.q: A strip of fabric is 2 14 m long. It is cut into pieces that are each 38 m long. How many pieces are there?
items.e: How many 38 m pieces fit in 2 14 m? Divide. Write 2 14 as 94. Keep 94, change ÷ to ×, and flip 38 to 83. Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and divide 8 and 4 by 4. Now 3 × 2 = 6 pieces. Check: 6 × 38 = 2 14.

items.q: A rectangular piece of fabric for a quilt is 34 m long and 23 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width. Simplify first: the 3s cancel, and divide 2 and 4 by 2. Now 12 × 1 = 12 m².

items.q: A hiking trail in Algonquin Park is 4 12 km long. Leah’s group has hiked 23 of the trail. How far has the group hiked?
items.e: 23 of 4 12 km means 23 × 4 12. Write 4 12 as 92. Simplify first: the 2s cancel, and divide 9 and 3 by 3. Now 1 × 3 = 3 km.

items.q: Benjamin hikes 2 14 km in 34 h. At this rate, how far does he hike in 1 h?
items.e: Divide the distance by the time. Write 2 14 as 94. Keep 94, change ÷ to ×, and flip 34 to 43. Simplify first: divide 9 and 3 by 3, and the 4s cancel. Now 3 × 1 = 3 km. Check: 3 × 34 = 2 14.

items.q: A trail is 2 12 km long. There is a bench at the end of every 58 km section. How many 58 km sections are there?
items.e: How many 58 km sections fit in 2 12 km? Divide. Write 2 12 as 52. Keep 52, change ÷ to ×, and flip 58 to 85. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and divide 8 and 2 by 2. Now 1 × 4 = 4 sections. Check: 4 × 58 = 2 12.

items.q: On a canoe trip, a portage is 1 15 km long. Noah carries the canoe for 56 of the portage. How far does he carry it?
items.e: 56 of 1 15 km means 56 × 1 15. Write 1 15 as 65. Simplify first: the 5s cancel, and the 6s cancel. Now 1 × 1 = 1 km.

items.q: There is 34 of a pizza left. Zoe eats 13 of what is left. What fraction of the whole pizza does she eat?
c: 14 of the pizza
49 of the pizza
47 of the pizza
1 112 of the pizza
items.e: 13 of 34 means 13 × 34. Simplify first: the 3s cancel. Now 1 × 14 = 14 of the pizza.

items.q: A jug holds 23 L of apple cider. Each glass holds 16 L. How many glasses can be filled?
items.e: How many 16 L glasses fit in 23 L? Divide. Keep 23, change ÷ to ×, and flip 16 to 6. Simplify first: divide 6 and 3 by 3. Now 2 × 2 = 4 glasses. Check: 4 × 16 = 23.

items.q: Emma uses 12 of a can of paint to paint 35 of a fence. How many cans does she need to paint the whole fence?
items.e: Paint for the whole fence = paint used ÷ fraction of the fence painted. Keep 12, change ÷ to ×, and flip 35 to 53. 12 × 53 = 1 × 52 × 3 = 56 can. Check: 56 × 35 = 12.

items.q: In a community garden plot, 58 of the area is vegetables. 25 of the vegetable area is tomatoes. What fraction of the plot is tomatoes?
c: 14 of the plot
713 of the plot
1625 of the plot
1 140 of the plot
items.e: 25 of 58 means 25 × 58. Simplify first: divide 2 and 8 by 2, and the 5s cancel. Now 1 × 14 = 14 of the plot.

items.q: 23 of the Grade 7 students go on a field trip to Ottawa. 34 of those students visit the Canadian Museum of Nature. What fraction of the Grade 7 students visit the museum?
c: 1 512 of the students
1 18 of the students
12 of the students
57 of the students
items.e: 34 of 23 means 34 × 23. Simplify first: the 3s cancel, and divide 2 and 4 by 2. Now 12 × 1 = 12 of the students.

items.q: A recipe for 12 muffins uses 1 13 cups of flour. Olivia makes 1 12 times the recipe. How much flour does she need?
items.e: 1 12 times 1 13 cups: multiply. Write 1 13 as 43. Write 1 12 as 32. Simplify first: divide 4 and 2 by 2, and the 3s cancel. Now 2 × 1 = 2 cups.

items.q: Liam has 2 12 cups of flour. One batch of cookies needs 23 cup. How many full batches can he make?
items.e: Write 2 12 as 52. Keep 52, change ÷ to ×, and flip 23 to 32. 52 × 32 = 5 × 32 × 2 = 154 = 3 34. Check: 3 34 × 23 = 2 12. Only full batches count, so he can make 3 batches.

items.q: A trail is 56 km long. A sign is placed at the end of every 112 km. Which expression gives the number of 112 km sections?
c: 56 − 112
112 ÷ 56
56 ÷ 112
56 × 112
items.e: The question asks how many 112 km sections fit in 56 km, so divide 56 by 112: 56 ÷ 112 = 56 × 12 = 10 sections.

items.q: Hana has biked 1 12 km. That is 35 of a trail. How long is the whole trail?
items.e: 35 of the trail is 1 12 km, so the whole trail is 1 12 ÷ 35. Write 1 12 as 32. Keep 32, change ÷ to ×, and flip 35 to 53. Simplify first: the 3s cancel. Now 12 × 5 = 52 = 2 12 km. Check: 2 12 × 35 = 1 12.

items.q: Maya practises piano for 34 h. She spends 23 of the time on scales. How long does she spend on scales?
items.e: 23 of 34 h means 23 × 34. Simplify first: divide 2 and 4 by 2, and the 3s cancel. Now 1 × 12 = 12 h. That is 30 min.
